Where I work, we are migrating users from Vista to 7, while also removing admin rights so that they can't reinstall all their shitty, virus-laden toolbars and such. The default games are also being removed. This is all because there is a standard being set, and as well Software Asset Management is becoming a thing. That is the team I am a part of.

Part of the rest of the team deals with making the software into packages that can just be quietly installed for users by pushing it through a software center.

I am currently just dispatching certain requests to them while taking other requests for myself.

The new request from this morning is that a user is missing all of the adobe suite after migration. Okay, maybe we don't have a package yet. This is where we got an assignment in the service request. We'll be working on this part.

Her print screen isn't working. Maybe she means she didn't get greenshot? Or maybe the keyboard is at fault? Either way, not my issue to fix, since that's been assigned to someone in deployment.

The last part in the overall request description is the one that had me drop my head on my desk. And laugh. A lot.

"Also, the PRINT SCREEN function and GAMES!!!!! On behalf of myself and every user of Spider Solitaire, can I/we pleeeeze have this game reinstalled. If Solitaire reinstall cannot be done, then can I buy a version of Solitaire and have it installed?"

I am fairly sure she will have been told no. It isn't part of the standard desktop, and she has only been on Windows 7 for a couple days at most.

But she did say pleeeeze so who knows?
